pairs.locus: Mirandola, Ad amicum excusatio quod amet 1-7
pairs.question: Quid me nequitiae damnas? quid dicis inertem quem premat imposito pulchra puella iugo? quid virides annos studiis melioribus aptos, quid frangi ingenium dicis, amice, meum? quod nec grande aliquid nec fortia bella capessam enerventque animos carmen et umbra meos?
pairs.answer: uror amans, fateor, sunt haec mea proelia, flammas nec volo nec possum dissimulare meas.
pairs.derivation: The poem opens with the friend's reproaches cast as a contiguous block of four interrogatives (quid me... quid dicis... quid virides... quid frangi... dicis), extended by the quod-clause that completes the final question (lines 3-6). Quoted the entire question span verbatim and contiguous. The poet's reply begins at 'uror amans, fateor' (line 7); the answer window is the first full sentence ending at 'meas' (line 8), which directly answers the charge ('I burn with love, I confess... I neither wish nor am able to conceal my flames'). Stopped there before he turns to elaborating his defense ('crimen at hoc certe nostrum...'). Stripped the title line, the trailing 'Mirandola / Neo-Latin / The Latin Library / The Classics Page' footer, and normalized terminal punctuation.
